title: Attribution ledger edge -- causal relation between two pieces of work
description: v2 (2026-08-25, Pavlo's mechanical-not-prose-only round): source_entry/target now reference schema.json's entry_id (a real, resolvable ledger entry) instead of a free-form id/commit/hash string, and the verified_application requirements are enforced via if/then instead of documented only in prose. A single ledger entry (schema.json) records ONE claim; this file is the causal edge between two of them -- a foundation discovery/audit/method DELIBERATELY APPLIED to a Vertice surface, or the reverse -- a Vertice/commercial surface that enabled foundation work to happen at all. Pavlo's framing, kept close to verbatim: 'contribution follows the reproduced causal edge, not repository location or commit authorship.'

edge_type.description: Closed enum. 'dependency': a surface uses a foundation artifact/tool without any deliberate, verified act of applying a specific discovery to it -- recorded, never counts. 'verified_application': a specific foundation discovery/audit/spec-correction/method was DELIBERATELY applied to a named Vertice surface, and that application itself was independently verified -- the only edge_type that can count. 'enabling_provenance': the reverse direction -- a Vertice/commercial surface enabled foundation work to exist -- recorded for an honest bidirectional causal graph, never sized, never counts.

source_entry.description: The `entry_id` (schema.json) this edge originates from -- a real, independently-verified ledger entry, not a free-form string. If the thing being applied/depended-on/enabling doesn't have a ledger entry yet, write that entry first; an edge cannot point at something unrecorded.

target.description: The `entry_id` (schema.json) of what the source was applied to, depends on, or enabled. Same rule as source_entry -- must be a real ledger entry's id, resolvable to that entry's own `surface` field, which is what `counts_toward_vertice_split` reads (see x-derivation-rule below). This is the concrete fix for Merlini's dinamic.eth/boiler-kit/ai.verticecriativo.pt case: recording that enabling_provenance edge requires a real ledger entry for the enabling surface to exist first (a `build` entry describing what it was and when), not a bare description inline on the edge.

edge_verified_by.description: REQUIRED and non-empty when edge_type is 'verified_application' (enforced below, not just documented); optional/absent otherwise. Verifies the CAUSAL LINK ITSELF -- that the application actually happened and actually caused the target -- a different, additional verification from whichever verified_by already exists on the source entry's own claim.

timestamp.description: When the causal relation is recorded (not necessarily when either endpoint's own entry was made). An actual event timestamp, not a round/approximate one.

source_contribution_ref.description: The exact foundation contribution being applied -- restates source_entry's own entry_id for readability, or points at the specific sub-part of it (a file, a function) that was actually applied. Required for verified_application.

target_surface_ref.description: The exact Vertice surface/feature/release/claim the contribution was applied to -- a commit, release tag, or product-facing reference, not a repo name alone. Required for verified_application.

causal_link_verification.description: How the causal link itself (not just the source claim) was independently confirmed -- what the edge_verified_by parties actually checked. Required for verified_application.

x-derivation-rule: counts_toward_vertice_split is NEVER a stored/writable field on an edge. A reader computes it: true iff ALL of -- (1) edge_type == 'verified_application', (2) edge_verified_by is present and non-empty, (3) evidence carries all three required refs (enforced by the if/then above, so a schema-valid verified_application edge always satisfies this), AND (4) resolving `target` to its ledger entry (schema.json) shows surface.classification == 'vertice_product' (v2 addition, Pavlo's ask -- a verified_application edge whose target is NOT a Vertice product surface, e.g. applied to a vendor's own repo or another external party's surface, must not count, and checking only edge_type + verified_by without resolving the target's actual surface was the v1 gap). Every other edge_type, or any edge whose target resolves to a non-vertice_product surface, is unconditionally false -- dependency and enabling_provenance are attribution, never sizing, no matter how well-evidenced.
